claims.statement: Retained: the finite-group quotient-flow lifting theorem is valid when the relation is invariant and nonnegative integer supplies and capacities are orbit-constant; the stated S3 wreath-product states and deletion/two-for-one adjacency describe T_m for every m>=1; and the pinned quotient flows yield valid complete-sum checks for the three specified (m,p) rows.
claims.scope: General finite-group lifting theorem under the stated hypotheses; structural orbit and adjacency description for the designated T_m family, m>=1; bounded flow applications only at (22,34), (60,90), and (66,98). No quotient feasibility at other parameters and no resolution of the arbitrary-tree aggregate.
claims.reason: retained — the invariant-maximizer argument proves the lift, the state multiplicities and relation transitions exhaust the T_m configurations, and scratch-copy replay verified exact selectors, guards, literal positive arcs, orbit capacities, saturation, and the complete sums in the three pinned rows. These finite examples do not establish a uniform flow family or the primary target.

limitations: The quotient-flow applications are bounded to (m,p)=(22,34),(60,90),(66,98); no all-m quotient-feasibility result was established.
The structural orbit and adjacency proof applies to the designated T_m family and the audited deletion-plus-exactly-two-neighbor relation.
This critique establishes no proof or counterexample for the arbitrary-tree lower-region aggregate.
